identity.display_name: Audi R8 LMS GT3 Evo II
identity.real_world_identity_notes: Audi identifies the Evo II as the second evolution of the R8 LMS GT3. The exact base AMS2 identity was guided-tested; the Low Downforce identity is an explicit aero-package alias inheriting the base controls and was not separately tested.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim without an integrated display or wheel-mounted shift lights.

notes: The base car moved from rest without physical clutch input; the underlying simulator mechanism was not established.
Six paddle-selected gears, clutchless no-lift upshifts, and clutchless downshifts with automatic blip were directly established.
A brief throttle-channel interruption was later found insufficient to establish automatic ignition cut; that field remains unknown.
The Low Downforce identity inherits base controls as an explicit untested aero-package assumption.

overrides.condition: The fingerprinted RSS v2 implementation stalled or refused move-off without physical clutch input, unlike the curated authentic and three other simulator observations.

confidence.basis: The guided move-off test directly observed that the car would not pull away with the physical clutch released while automatic clutch and shifting assists were disabled.

overrides.condition: The fingerprinted RSS v2 implementation exhibited an automatic shift cut that is not established for the real car or the other reviewed simulators.

confidence.basis: The guided AC drive directly detected the implementation's automatic cut from a torque collapse under sustained throttle.

The fingerprinted RSS v2 package is a German 501 hp V10 GT3 with the Audi R8 LMS wheelbase, track and weight envelope. Its bundled `#1 Scherer Sport PHX Farewell Audi` livery explicitly loads Audi badge assets. RSS's first-party product data and the installed package therefore converge on the Audi R8 LMS GT3 Evo II, while the AC behavior and cockpit were directly observed.

claims.basis: Official simulator and manufacturer sources agree with the exact live telemetry identity and class.
Low Downforce is an exact observed identity whose controls explicitly inherit the tested base as an aero-package assumption.
Audi lineage documentation and direct exercise of all six paddle-selected gears agree.
Guided current-game testing and cockpit inspection directly established these values.

Assetto Corsa EVO reports the car as "Audi R8 LMS GT3 Evo II", which differs only in the case of "Evo" from the AMS2 name for the same car and is recorded as its own identity rather than assumed to match.

SimHub simultaneously reported telemetry name `Audi R8 LMS Evo II 2022`, internal id `audi_r8_lms_evo_ii`, and class `GT3`, so this is the same 2022 Evo II already curated from Audi, AMS2 and AC EVO evidence rather than a nearby R8 generation.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic blip, and the cockpit rim; automatic cut remained unknown.

RSS identifies the exact GT-M Aero V10 Evo2 v2 implementation. The matching installed package names Scherer Sport PHX's Farewell Audi livery, includes Audi badge configuration, reports Germany and GT3, and matches the Audi's V10 architecture and dimensions. These implementation-specific facts map the fictionalized name to the existing Audi R8 LMS GT3 Evo II record without treating the mod name itself as a real-car identity.

notes: Low Downforce is an explicit inherited alias and was not separately live-tested.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
